# Every-Site Scraping

> Parallel Python web scraper **and crawler** that turns any list of URLs — or a
> single seed site — into one 90-column row per page: SEO metadata, Open Graph,
> contact details, social profiles, JSON-LD and tech stack. Outputs CSV, typed
> JSON, append-only JSONL or queryable SQLite. Crash-safe resume, robots-aware,
> flat memory at any site count.

Every-Site Scraping is a Python 3.8+ command-line tool and library for **bulk
website data extraction**. It accepts an arbitrary list of URLs (arguments, a
`.txt` file, stdin, or a CSV/lead-export with an auto-detected website column) or
a seed site to crawl, then scrapes everything in parallel with 10–40+ workers.
Each page becomes exactly one row across a fixed 90-column schema.

## Commands

- `scrape` — scrape an explicit URL list into a dataset
- `crawl` — discover URLs by following links + sitemaps, then scrape them
- `discover` — crawl only; print the discovered URL list
- `probe` — inspect a site's robots.txt, sitemaps and HTTP behaviour
- `audit` — validate an output file (csv/json/jsonl/sqlite)
- `schema` — print the 90-column schema
- `init` — write a commented `scraper.toml`
- `config` — print the effective merged configuration

Library API: `from everysite import scrape, crawl, discover, SCHEMA`

## What it extracts

- **Identity & request**: final URL, HTTP status, page title, domain, site name
- **Meta & Open Graph**: meta description, keywords, OG title/description/image/type/locale
- **Twitter cards**: card type, title, description, image, handle
- **SEO**: canonical URL, robots meta, viewport, language, charset, favicon, generator
- **Content**: H1 text and heading counts, word count, character count, rendering type
- **Links & assets**: internal/external/total links, image, document, media, script and stylesheet URLs (absolute, deduped, sorted)
- **Social & contact**: social profile links plus contact emails and phone numbers (visible text, mailto/tel, and JSON-LD)
- **Organization**: org name, description, logo, URL, founding date, location, phone, JSON-LD types
- **Tech & weight**: HTTPS, detected technologies with evidence, page size in bytes, response time in ms

## Key capabilities

- **Crawling** — link following with depth control, `/sitemap.xml` and
  robots-declared sitemap expansion (including nested indexes), registrable-domain
  or exact-host scope, include/exclude regexes, and deterministic URL order
- **Honest robots.txt** — honoured by default including `Crawl-delay`; disallowed
  URLs are counted in the summary rather than silently dropped
- **URL canonicalisation** — strips tracking parameters, default ports, fragments
  and duplicate slashes so the same page is scraped once
- **Politeness** — a per-host minimum request interval (`--delay`) plus the site's
  own `Crawl-delay`, while different hosts run in parallel
- **Proxy rotation** — a pool from a file, rotated round-robin with dead-proxy
  quarantine
- **Retries with backoff** — on 202/429/5xx and timeouts, jittered
- **Four output formats** — CSV, typed JSON, append-only JSONL, SQLite (indexed on url)
- **Parallel engine** — N workers pull from one queue; per-worker counts appear in
  the run summary (verified, not claimed)
- **Crash-safe resume** — every completed row is flushed and fsynced immediately;
  `--resume` continues exactly where a killed run stopped, in any format
- **Honest failure reporting** — HTTP 200 with an empty body is reported as
  `empty_response`, never as success
- **Fixed 90-column schema** — `csv.DictWriter(extrasaction="raise")` makes a
  malformed row raise instead of shifting columns
- **Flat memory** — RAM scales with `--workers`, not with the number of sites

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zaktecs-ai/every-site-scraping.git
cd every-site-scraping
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Dependencies: `requests`, `beautifulsoup4`, `lxml`. Python 3.8+.
Optionally `pip install .` to get the `every-site-scraping` / `esscrape` commands.

## Quick start

```bash
# scrape a few sites
python -m everysite scrape https://www.python.org https://www.postgresql.org

# 500 sites from a file — 30 workers
python -m everysite scrape -f sites.csv -o out.csv -w 30 --json

# crawl a site then scrape every page found
python -m everysite crawl https://example.com -d 2 -n 500 -o site.csv

# crawl straight into SQLite
python -m everysite crawl https://example.com -d 2 -o site.sqlite

# continue an interrupted run (works for csv/json/jsonl/sqlite)
python -m everysite scrape -f sites.csv -o out.csv -w 30 --resume
```

## Validation

163 unit tests (Python 3.8–3.13, plus macOS and Windows in CI). Measured on a
2-core machine: 126 distinct live sites scraped at 96.8% success in 84.7 s
(89 sites/min); a real `SIGKILL` at 221/400 rows followed by `--resume` completed
the exact 179 remaining with zero duplicates and zero loss.

## Responsible use

You are responsible for what you fetch. Respect each site's terms of service and
applicable law, keep request rates reasonable, and note that `robots.txt` is
honoured by default.
